name: TS3A24159DRCR
title: 0.3 Ω dual SPDT bidirectional analog switch
summary: Two independent single-pole double-throw switches, each a 2:1 multiplexer or demultiplexer that conducts either way, running from a single 1.65 V to 3.6 V supply. ON resistance is 0.3 Ω at most at 25 °C on a 2.7 V supply, with break-before-make action, low charge injection and low distortion. The control inputs accept 1.8 V logic. Offered in 10-pin VSSOP, VSON and DSBGA packages.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A system controller on a 3.3 V rail steers two signals through the switch. Its two logic outputs drive IN1 and IN2; its signal lines run to COM1 and COM2, and each COM reaches one of two devices: COM1 to Device 1 on NO1 or Device 2 on NC1, COM2 to Device 3 on NO2 or Device 4 on NC2. The controller and the switch each have a 0.1 µF capacitor from the 3.3 V rail to ground; both share ground.

circuits.title: ON-state resistance test
circuits.description: A DC source is applied through a selector to NC or NO, a current source pulls ICOM out of COM, and a fixed logic level on IN closes the channel under test. ron is the COM-to-NC or COM-to-NO voltage over ICOM.

parts.note: applies the source to NC or to NO

circuits.title: OFF-state leakage current test
circuits.description: With the channel open, one DC source sits on NC or NO through a selector and a second DC source holds COM; the current into the open terminal is the OFF leakage.

parts.note: applies the source to NC or to NO

circuits.title: ON-state leakage current test
circuits.description: With the channel closed, a DC source sits on NC or NO through a selector and COM is left open; the current flowing at the driven terminal is the ON leakage.

parts.note: applies the source to NC or to NO

circuits.title: Capacitance test
circuits.description: A capacitance meter, its bias at VCC or GND, connects through a switch to NO; COM and IN are brought out and IN is held at VIH or VIL. Capacitance is read at NO, COM and IN with the channel ON and OFF.

circuits.title: Turn-on and turn-off time test
circuits.description: COM is held at VCC. NC and NO each drive a 50 Ω load with 35 pF to ground. A logic pulse from 0 to VCC on IN switches the channel; tON and tOFF run from the 50% point of the logic edge to the 90% point of the output at NC or NO.

parts.note: logic input VI; PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr and tf < 5 ns

circuits.title: Break-before-make time test
circuits.description: NC and NO are tied together at VCC; COM drives 50 Ω with 35 pF to ground. When a logic pulse on IN moves the switch, COM dips while neither throw conducts; tBBM is the time between the output's 90% points on its way down and back up.

parts.note: logic input VI; PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr and tf < 5 ns

circuits.title: Bandwidth test
circuits.description: A network analyzer's 50 Ω source drives NC with the NC-to-COM channel closed by a DC level on IN; COM returns to the analyzer's 50 Ω input. Source power is 0 dBm (632 mV peak to peak into 50 Ω) on a 350 mV DC bias.

circuits.title: OFF isolation test
circuits.description: The analyzer's 50 Ω source drives NC, which is also terminated by 50 Ω to ground, with the NC-to-COM channel held open by IN; COM feeds the analyzer's 50 Ω input. Source power is 0 dBm on a 350 mV DC bias.

circuits.title: Crosstalk test
circuits.description: The analyzer's 50 Ω source drives NC through the closed NC-to-COM channel; COM is terminated by 50 Ω to ground. NO, on the open throw, feeds the analyzer's 50 Ω input. Source power is 0 dBm on a 350 mV DC bias.

circuits.title: Charge injection test
circuits.description: A DC source VGEN (0 to VCC) drives NC or NO through RGEN = 0; COM is loaded by CL = 1 nF. A logic pulse on IN turns the channel on and off, and the step ΔVCOM it leaves on CL gives QC = CL × ΔVCOM.

parts.note: logic input VI; PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr and tf < 5 ns

circuits.title: Total harmonic distortion test
circuits.description: An audio analyzer's source (600 Ω, VCC peak to peak, 20 Hz to 20 kHz) is terminated by 600 Ω and AC-coupled through 10 µF into COM, with the COM-to-NO channel closed. NO is biased to V+/2 through RL = 600 Ω, loaded by CL = 50 pF, and AC-coupled through 10 µF to the analyzer's 600 Ω input.

where.ICOM: current forced through the closed channel

where.ΔVCOM: step on COM when the switch is toggled

operation.text: The two switches are independent, each set by its own logic input. IN low closes COM to NC; IN high closes COM to NO. Every terminal conducts in both directions, so NO, NC and COM each serve as input or output. Break-before-make is specified: the closed throw opens before the other closes (tBBM 0.5 ns minimum over temperature at 3 V).

IN1 and IN2 accept 1.8 V logic: VIH is 1 V minimum and VIL 0.4 V maximum at VCC = 1.65 V to 1.95 V, rising to 1.4 V and 0.5 V at 2.7 V to 3.6 V. The digital input absolute maximum is 3.6 V. Unused control inputs are held at VCC or GND, and IN1 and IN2 are pulled up or down so that a floating pin cannot set an unintended switch position.

Signals on NO, NC and COM run from 0 V to VCC, so the supply is chosen to cover the whole swing of the signal being switched. Absolute maximum on a signal pin is VCC + 0.5 V, never above 5.5 V. Continuous switch current is rated ±300 mA, and ±500 mA peak in 1 ms pulses at under 10% duty.
No external components are needed for the switch to work. Unused pins are tied to ground through 50 Ω so that signals are not reflected back into the device.

VCC is brought up before any signal is applied to NO or COM. Bypassing is optional but improves noise margin and stops switching noise spreading from the VCC supply to other components; 0.1 µF from VCC to GND suits most uses.

Supplies carry bypass capacitors, and traces are kept short to avoid loading. An 0603 capacitor sits at the VCC pin with a via to the ground plane, and the GND pin has its own via to the ground plane. The VSON thermal pad is soldered to the board.
Latch-up exceeds 100 mA per JESD 78, Class II. ESD is tested per JESD 22 to 2000 V human-body model (A114-B, Class II) and 1000 V charged-device model (C101).
